angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 716,571 km at 90.05 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.1052 +/- 0.0175 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 90.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.03 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-8 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 716,571 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.34 +/- 0.26 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-8 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5600 +/- 80 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-8 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-8 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-8.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.539, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-8 (pscomppars): spectral type G8 V, from Salz et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015A&A...576A..42S/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, CD-35 16019: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-8 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.17 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-8 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.05754, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-8 (pscomppars): age 3 Gyr, from Borsato et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.506.3810B/abstract)
